stem: The same packaged product is stored in two areas, but one area experiences large daily temperature swings. What is the best quality-control response?
choices: Treat the packaging as the primary control and compare only the final product results after the storage period ends.
Track actual storage conditions and compare product-quality trends between locations.
Standardize the inspection schedule but avoid linking storage records to the individual locations being compared.
Adjust the cultivation nutrient program to reduce quality variation that may appear during later storage.
rationale: Storage temperature history can affect product stability. Environmental records linked to batch identity support meaningful comparison and investigation.
